ai_metadata.description_ai: A magnificent marble building built in memory of Queen Victoria, now a museum showcasing India's colonial history and artifacts.
A 19th-century temple dedicated to Goddess Kali, located on the Hooghly River, associated with the mystic Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
A massive cantilever bridge without nuts and bolts, spanning the Hooghly River and symbolizing Kolkata's industrial heritage.
The vibrant heart of Darjeeling, a pedestrian stretch lined with colonial buildings, shops, cafes, and stunning Kanchenjunga views.
The highest point near Darjeeling, famous for spectacular sunrise views over Mount Kanchenjunga and even Mount Everest on clear days.
A UNESCO World Heritage narrow-gauge railway, winding through picturesque hills and tea gardens with a historic steam locomotive.
The world's largest mangrove forest and UNESCO site, home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, crocodiles, and diverse bird species.
A prime entry point to the Sundarbans with a watchtower, museum, crocodile park, and mangrove interpretation center.
Famous for unique terracotta temples with intricate carvings depicting scenes from Hindu mythology.
A twin temple with exquisite terracotta carvings, built in 1655 with a roof resembling a traditional Bengali hut.
A town founded by Rabindranath Tagore, home to Visva-Bharati University, known for its artistic and literary heritage.
A quiet hill station known for its Buddhist monasteries, flower nurseries, and panoramic views of the Teesta River.
A Buddhist monastery on Durpin Hill, consecrated by the Dalai Lama, offering breathtaking views of the Teesta River.
The most popular beach in West Bengal, stretching 7 km along the Bay of Bengal with water sports and sunset views.
An extension of Digha Beach with cleaner waters, wider sands, and various water sports activities like jet skiing and parasailing.
A serene hill town centered around Sumendu Lake, offering boating, horse riding, and stunning mountain views.
A grand palace with a thousand doors, built in the 19th century, now a museum showcasing Nawabi artifacts and weapons.
The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda, with architecture blending Hindu, Islamic, and Christian styles.
The gateway to Northeast India, a bustling city surrounded by tea gardens and offering access to hill stations.
A beautiful ISKCON temple with stunning architecture, peaceful atmosphere, and a vegetarian restaurant.
A national park known for its Indian one-horned rhinoceros, elephants, and diverse birdlife in the Dooars region.
A wildlife park famous for its one-horned rhinoceros population and elephant safari experiences.
A Gothic-style Anglican cathedral from the 19th century, known for its beautiful stained-glass windows and serene atmosphere.
The oldest and largest museum in India, housing collections of art, archaeology, anthropology, and natural history.
A 19th-century mansion with marble floors, sculptures, paintings, and antique furniture, still privately owned.
The ancestral home of the Tagore family, now a museum dedicated to the life and works of Rabindranath Tagore.
